newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Dec corn sets fresh 14 month low on estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Dec corn sets fresh 14 month low on estimate.

text.p: CBOT December corn dropped to a fresh 14-month low on bearish reaction to a private crop estimate, traders said.

Iowa-based analytical firm Farmers Commodities Corp Monday said the 1996 U.S. corn crop would total 9.33 billion bushels, above trade expectations for 9.2 billion and USDA's forecast in October for 9.012 billion.
"People on the floor were looking for a 9.2, so FCC was a little bearish," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA on November 12 will release its next crop estimate, and several more private estimates are expected out this week.

The new harvest low, which also is the fresh 14-month low for December, was $2.57-3/4 per bushel as of 1135 CST. That was the lowest price seen for that contract since $2.57-1/4 was hit on August 11, 1995.
Traders also said the market remains technically weak with the key moving averages tilting downward.
December broke below first support at $2.60 and was trading between that level and second support seen at $2.55-1/2.
At 1135 CST, corn was three to 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 3-1/2 at $2.58-1/4.
